Writes to console/patches/, never to the game's files, the generated runner/*.cpp or headers. Use when the user says "mod this game", "add a cheat", "infinite health", "port this pnach", "make my gun do X", "change how X works", "game override", "turn this PCSX2 patch into the port", or once the port boots and they want to change it.

Physics Tuner. Finds the numbers that decide how the game moves (speed, gravity, grip, jump height, frame rate) and tunes them. Scans the user's own game ELF for a float32 value stored in data or built in code (lui, ori or addiu, then mtc1), shows the instructions that read it, lists frame-timing candidates, and prints the exact pnach lines to test a new value in PCSX2 plus the PS2Recomp fix (TOML instruction patches or the data write /console-mod bakes in). Reads only; writes nothing. Use when the user says "make the car faster", "lower the gravity", "jump higher", "more grip", "change the damage", "wider camera", "unlock 60 fps", "find the speed value", or when /console-mod needs a number found.

Reverse Engineer. Opens your own disc image, finds the game's code and maps how it works: the boot ELF, every function, the design doc. Drives the whole port and is the entry point of the Console pack. Reads ISO 9660 images without loading them whole, reads SYSTEM.CNF and the boot ELF (segments, CRC-32 and PCSX2 CRC, IRX modules), writes a starter PS2Recomp TOML with real keys only, and keeps console/STATE.md, the memory every /console-* skill reads first. Carries the PS2Recomp rules: never clean the build, never edit generated code or headers, a build gate, and a three-strike circuit breaker. Use when the user says "port my PS2 game", "recompile my game", "open my ISO", "what's on this disc", "set up PS2Recomp", "where are we", "continue the port", or at the start of any Console session.

Save Manager. Brings your old memory card saves over, backs them up and syncs them to the cloud so you continue on any device. Reads PS2 memory card images (PCSX2 .ps2 and .mcd, raw 8 MB dumps, with or without ECC) and PCSX2 folder cards, lists every save with its title, copies saves into the port's folder memory card (mc0 next to the game's ELF), imports and exports single saves as .psu, makes timestamped zip backups, and syncs mc0 with an iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Google Drive or Syncthing folder. Card images are read only; mc0 is backed up before anything replaces a save; a sync never silently overwrites (when both sides changed it keeps both and reports a conflict). Use when the user says "bring my saves over", "import my PCSX2 save", "my memory card", "back up my saves", "sync my saves", "continue on my Steam Deck", "restore a backup", "convert this .psu", or before the first run of a port that needs a save.

Sound Designer. Rips the music and sound effects and puts your own tracks back in. Decodes PS2 VAG files and raw SPU2 ADPCM from sound banks (.bd) to WAV, finds VAGs hidden inside archives and disc files, and encodes your own 16-bit WAV back to VAG at the original's sample rate, looping and size. Playtester. Runs the port again and again, reads every crash, ranks what to fix next and checks nothing broke. run.py starts ps2EntryRunner with your game's ELF under a hard timeout, kills the whole process tree, keeps the log in console/runs/ and calls the run PASS, HANG, CRASH or FAIL (soak repeats it N times; --input replays a controller script). triage.py reads the runtime's own log lines, clusters them by PC, names the function from your Ghidra CSV map, ranks them and names the /console-* skill that owns each; compare shows fixed, still there and new. abdiff.py finds the first divergence between PCSX2 and the port in register or memory dumps. Use when the user says "run it", "does it boot", "test the port", "why did it crash", "what do I fix next", "did that break anything", "run it 100 times", "compare with PCSX2", or after every build.
